title: API Key Usage Explorer — wireframe & backlog notes
body:
Context and goal:

Quick exploratory notes for a new Console screen: API Key Usage Explorer. Purpose: give engineers and platform owners a fast per-key, per-route breakdown of consumption (tokens, requests, latency) plus quick controls for rate-limits and quota overrides. This is an early design + grooming doc for PM/design/eng alignment.

High level product questions (to resolve):
- Who is primary persona: API owner (platform) vs app developer? Assume both; primary persona is the API owner who needs to troubleshoot spikes and enforce budgets.
- Data latency SLA: near-real-time (1-5m) for last 24h, hourly rollups beyond that. Check infra cost.
- Enforcement vs visibility: we need paths for read-only views vs direct editing of limits.

Wireframe notes (page sections) — rough left-to-right flow:
1) Top filter bar (sticky)
   - Time range picker: last 1h / 6h / 24h / 7d / custom
   - Scope selector: Org / Team / Key (typeahead)
   - Route filter: route name or tag, supports wildcards (e.g. /chat/* )
   - Quick metric selector: tokens | requests | errors | p50/p95 latency
   - Apply / Reset buttons and an "Open in Insights" link to full analytics.

2) Key summary strip (horizontal cards) — shows for selected key (or aggregated):
   - Key label + owner + creation date (small)
   - Current rate limit (requests/s) and quota (monthly tokens) with colored health indicator (green/yellow/red).
   - 24h totals: tokens, requests, errors, avg latency.
   - Estimated bill delta: delta vs last period (simple $ estimate).
   - Quick action buttons: Edit limits (pencil), Pause key (pause icon), Create Ticket (link).

3) Per-route table (primary focus)
   Columns: Route | Calls (24h) | Tokens (24h) | Avg tokens/call | Errors | p50/p95 latency | Current route limit | Suggested quantization | Notes
   - Each row is expandable to show sparkline (1h resolution) and top example requests (scrubbed).
   - Inline actions: set per-route limit (number input), pin route (for alerts), tag route (e.g. webhook, batch), open deep-inspect.

4) Right rail panels (contextual)
   - Route detail: usage histogram, breakdown by model variant (if applicable), sample prompt shapes (token length distribution).
   - Cost impact simulator: adjust batching/quantization or change model -> live estimate of monthly cost.
   - Audit events: recent changes to this key (who changed limits).

5) Global analytics chart area (collapsible)
   - Topline timeseries for selected metric with multi-series (key, top 3 routes). Click series -> table filter.

Micro-interactions and UX patterns:
- Editing limits: click pencil -> small modal with current limit, recommended limit (algorithmic suggestion), risk note (SLA impact), "Apply (dry-run)" checkbox that will preview alerts but not enforce.
- Dry-run mode: shows predicted enforcement breaches for next 24h based on trend. Useful for conservative rollouts.
- Inline help: hover tokens -> tooltip explaining token counting rules and embeddings cost nuance.
- Error highlighting: rows with >1% error rate get amber badge; >5% red with an expand prompt showing sample error types (rate limit exceeded, timeout, model error).
- Bulk actions: multi-select rows to set uniform per-route limit or tag routes for batching optimization.

Telemetry mapping (what to show and where it comes from):
- Requests: raw request count by route/key from proxy logs (1m/5m agg)
- Tokens: renderer + serving runtime token accounting (should tie to billing).
- Latency: p50/p95 from downstream APM + serving runtime traces; combine but surface serving-only and end-to-end toggles.
- Errors: categorize by rejection vs runtime vs client error.
- Suggestions: offline Optimize service provides suggested quantization/batch size per route.

Privacy/security notes:
- Never show raw prompts in preview; only token-length histogram and redacted examples.
- Only show keys to users with appropriate IAM role. For non-admins, hide estimated bill delta.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- View time-range filtered per-key summary + per-route table with counts and token totals (24h and 7d).
- Able to set per-route rate limit and have change recorded in audit log.
- Inline sparkline + expand for last 60m at 1m resolution.
- Export CSV of per-route metrics for selected key.
- RBAC: only owners or billing roles see cost estimates.

Nice-to-have (post-MVP backlog):
- Cost impact simulator with model switching and batching toggles.
- Dry-run enforcement analysis and automated rollout (canary limits).
- Alerts templating from a pinned route (generate Slack message + Linear ticket).

Backlog grooming (priority order) — rough effort estimate and owner initials:
1) Data plumbing: expose aggregated per-key/per-route metrics in Metrics API (2w) — owner: JonP — blocking.
2) Per-route table UI & expand row details (1.5w) — owner: ElenaR.
3) Edit limits modal + audit write path (1w) — owner: SamirD.
4) RBAC gating for cost fields (0.5w) — owner: PM/infra security.
5) CSV export (0.5w) — owner: frontend.
6) Cost estimate microservice hookup (2w) — owner: backend.
7) Right-rail cost simulator (1w) — dependent on #6.

Open questions / risks:
- How expensive is 1m resolution for all keys? Need to set sane default and limit retention. Potential mitigation: 1m for last 2h, 5m for 24h, hourly beyond that.
- Model of suggested limits: ML suggestions may overfit — include human-in-loop with recommended confidence score.
- Multi-tenant privacy: ensure cross-Org isolation when owners query aggregated views.

Design TODOs (for next session):
- Finalize table column prioritization for small screens (mobile/ tablet).
- Sketch prioritization for keyboard-first workflows (keyboard nav for power users).
- Decide default sort order (tokens desc vs requests desc) and provide persisted user preference.

Notes to eng (hand-off checklist):
- Metrics API contract: provide samples for 1m/5m/1h rollups, include model_variant label, route tag, key id.
- Audit log events required: limit_change {old,new,actor,reason}, key_pause_resume {actor}, route_pin_unpin.
- Rate limit enforcement: need a feature-flagged path for immediate vs scheduled enforcement.

Next steps:
- Share with SRE/serving runtime to validate feasibility of 1m rollups.
- Quick frontend spike: static table + mock metrics for demo to PM/CS.
- Book cross-team grooming (design + infra + backend) for Sept sprint planning.

Quick links / references in doc:
- CON-2121 (Linear): API Usage explorer initial data schema
- Confluence: API Usage Schema (linked above)

Timestamped notes:
- 2025-09-15: initial draft and sketch by Maya.
- 2025-09-19: added cost-simulator idea after sync with Elena.
- 2025-10-02: updated acceptance criteria per SRE notes (reduced 1m retention window).
